title: Development and evaluation of machine learning models for voxel dose predictions in online adaptive magnetic resonance guided radiation therapy
summary: Artificial neural networks predicted patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from target and organ-at-risk structures for online adaptive MR-guided radiotherapy. Cross-validation on plans from 53 patients showed agreement with selected dose metrics and flagged 25 plans as potentially inferior. The retrospective planning analysis did not test effects on treatment decisions or patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Artificial neural networks predict patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from anatomical structures

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Cross-validation on more than 300 abdominal-cancer treatment plans reported R² values of 0.97, 0.95 and 0.95 for V95, V100 and D95; prediction intervals identified about 10% (25) of plans as lower quality.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective plan analysis; clinical integration and improved patient outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Artificial neural networks predict patient-specific three-dimensional dose distributions from anatomical structures
